The notation $(fg)(x)$ means  the product of the functions  $f(x)$ and $g(x).$

**Method 1**

To evaluate $(fg)(1),$ we find $f(1)$ and $g(1),$ and then multiply the results.

First, we find $f(1)$ and $g(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =8(1)^{2}+1=9 \\ g(1) & =2(1)-2=0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we multiply the results:

$$
(fg)(1)=f(1)g(1)=9\cdot 0=0
$$

**Method 2**

First, we find $(fg)(x)$ by multiplying the two functions:

$$
\begin{aligned}(fg)(x) & =(8{x}^{2}+1)(2x-2) \\  & =16{x}^{3}-16{x}^{2}+2x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate $(fg)(1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(fg)(1) & =16(1)^{3}-16(1)^{2}+2(1)-2 \\  & =16-16+2-2 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
